label: Command Center — OPC UA Server
info:
Command Center OPC UA Server + loopback OPC UA Client (subscribe).

Namespace ns=1
Variables per line (LINE-01 / LINE-02 / LINE-03):
  - <Line>.Request  (String, server-only convention — line-das only reads)
  - <Line>.Ack      (String, writable — line-das writes back here)

Clients (line-das) connect via:
  opc.tcp://command-center:5160/UA/CommandCenter

The loopback OPC UA Client subscribes to the three Ack variables so we can
receive client writes. (node-red-contrib-opcua's OpcUa-Server does not emit
client writes on its output wire in 0.2.351 — verified empirically.)

DB integration is handled by Picker (PR13) and AckHandler (PR14).

label: Picker — CommandDB poll → OPC UA write
info:
Picker flow (PR15).

Polls public.command_request (CommandDB) at 1 Hz. Atomically picks at most one
row per line via DISTINCT ON + FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, while skipping lines that
already have a PICKED/SENT command in flight. The single UPDATE...RETURNING in
the CTE writes:
    status      = 'SENT'
    worker_id   = $1   (env WORKER_ID, default 'command-center')
    picked_at   = now()
    started_at  = now()
and returns the picked rows (id, command_id, line_id, request_json).

For each returned row, we write the (already wire-compatible) request_json to
ns=1;s=Line-0X.Request on the OPC UA Server. line-das clients subscribed to
that variable then process the command and write the Ack back.

Note: FSM in CONTRACT.md lists REQUESTED → PICKED → SENT as separate steps.
We collapse PICKED → SENT into one UPDATE here because (a) the actual OPC UA
write happens immediately after, (b) both timestamps are set anyway. If the
OPC UA write fails the row stays SENT until the timeout sweeper (PR17)
reclaims it. PICKED-without-SENT is not an observable state in this
implementation.
